newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenya licenses opposition-backed rally in Mombasa.
newsitem.headline: Kenya licenses opposition-backed rally in Mombasa.

text.p: Kenya's government licensed on Friday an opposition-backed rally in the Indian Ocean city of Mombasa called for Saturday, greatly reducing the chances of renewed clashes between police and demonstrators.
"We have decided to licence tomorrow's rally following discussions between Sheikh (Khalil) Balala and me," Mombasa District Commissioner Peter Olando told Reuters in the city.
Balala is an Islamic preacher in Mombasa and perhaps the most outspoken critic in Kenya of President Daniel arap Moi.

Olando said Balala visited him at his office on Friday to tell him about the rally but had not requested a licence. But based on their talks, Olando decided it should be licensed and had issued a rally licence in the name of Balala, he added.
The government move greatly reduced the chances of a repeat in Mombasa of violent clashes elsewhere in Kenya in June and July between riot police and demonstrators demanding political reforms.
Mombasa is the centre of Kenya's coast tourism industry, the country's main employer and its largest earner of foreign exchange. It is also Kenya's second city and its main port.
At least nine people were killed on July 7 in Nairobi and several other cities and towns during violent clashes between police and demonstrators, Kenya's worst political violence for seven years.
Opposition-backed groups which called Saturday's rally had said they would not apply for any licences for their rallies on the grounds that the law requiring them was unconstitutional.
Moi said on July 16 that licences for opposition rallies would automatically be granted except in exceptional cases. But it remained a requirement for a licence to be applied for in advance.
Diplomats said on Friday a total of 22 foreign embassies and high commissions in Kenya had urged Moi in a letter to pursue dialogue with the opposition to avoid more political violence.
The reforms demanded by the opposition would cut the power of President Moi, 73 and in power for 19 years. No date is set for presidential and parliamentary polls this year.

The letter praised Moi for "demonstrating leadership" by meeting opposition and church leaders this month and said they supported Moi's directive that requests for political meetings be granted automatically.
Britain said on Wednesday it would reduce aid to Kenya if the government continued to crack down on demands for change.
The government allowed Balala to return to Kenya on July 12 from three years of forced exile in Germany after granting him a new passport and dropping its argument that he was not a Kenyan citizen.

The National Convention Executive Council (NCEC), the alliance of opposition parties, civic groups and other bodies demanding constitutional reforms, had said it hoped the Mombasa rally would be peaceful.

But after days of wrangling with authorities over who would be involved in any dialogue on reforms, some NCEC members said the only way ahead was to resume pressure on the government through more conflict between riot police and demonstrators.

The ruling KANU party headed by Moi announced on July 17 the government would set up a commission to recommend constitutional reforms and would repeal or ammend 11 laws the opposition had demanded scrapped before the general election.
